G14 cannot simply be copied by filling its unknown slots. This does not require every SUPPOSE to use G14: G02 permits a hypothetical frame, whose other content is still unbound. For RF, direct G14 alignment instead reaches fixed ar RECIPIENT at G009 where OUTPUT would be required; its grouping remains literal.

Each reader has SUPPOSE at .18/.24 and BUT at .22. Under a newly assumed linear .1-through-.24 traversal with mandatory one-to-one closure, the final frame would lack a later BUT. That traversal and closure convention were not owned. Nesting/reset/end-of-program/multi-frame closure are not supplied by the frozen grammar either. Count alone is not FAIL; a concrete frame-lifetime contract is needed.

ZL/IT .24 G008-G009 and RF G009-G010 give RECIPIENT HONEY. Both are kind terms, not a predicate/argument pair for G21. The first may complete a preceding expression and the second start a new one; missing boundaries and surrounding unknowns prevent a hard clash.

IT .24 G013-G015 and RF G014-G016 read RECIPIENT RECIPIENT YIELD. There is no inherited NOM type rule. Adjacent recipient nouns do not themselves create a proposition, comparison or apposition. G10 additionally needs reception scope and a following ProductKind; .24 line end supplies none. Nonlinear continuation is unowned, so a page-end unsaturation FAIL is not justified.
